session_note: The 132nd Maine Legislature's Second Regular Session adjourned sine die on 2026-04-29 at 8:32 PM (per mainelegislature.org/house/house/ and web.legislature.maine.gov), concluding the two-year (2025-2026) term of this Legislature. Maine allows carry-over of bills between the First Regular Session (2025) and Second Regular Session (2026) of the same Legislature via a Carry Over vote (used for several bills below in 2025), but nothing survives past this sine die into the 133rd Legislature; unfinished bills die on adjournment absent a special session. No 2026 special session affecting these bills was found.

evidence.title: LD 307, HP 207, Text and Status, 132nd Legislature
evidence.supports: Official Maine Legislature bill status page confirms sponsor (Rep. Gattine of Westbrook), amendment history (C-A H-881, H-A to C-A H-969/H-1051, etc.), Governor's veto on 2026-04-24, and final disposition 'Veto Sustained, Apr 29, 2026'.
evidence.quote: Governor's Action: Veto, Apr 24, 2026 ... Final Disposition: Veto Sustained, Apr 29, 2026

evidence.title: Maine House Roll Call No. 790, LD 307, Enactment, 4/8/2026
evidence.supports: Official House roll call showing the pre-veto enactment vote: Yes 83, No 66, votes required 75, motion prevails.
evidence.quote: MOTION: Enactment VOTES REQUIRED: 75 YES: 83 NO: 66 NV: 1 ... MOTION: PREVAILS

evidence.title: Maine House Roll Call No. 828, LD 307, veto override reconsideration, 4/29/2026
evidence.supports: Confirms the House veto-override attempt failed: Yeas 72, Nays 65, 92 needed (two-thirds), motion failed, sustaining the veto.
evidence.quote: Yeas (Y): 72 ... Nays (N): 65 ... required 92 yeas to pass but achieved only 72 affirmative votes

evidence.title: Governor Mills' veto message on L.D. 307
evidence.supports: Confirms the 2026-04-24 veto and Governor Mills' stated rationale (support for the moratorium concept generally, but objection to the bill's failure to exempt an already-permitted Jay, Maine data center redevelopment project).
evidence.quote: A moratorium is appropriate given the impacts of massive data centers in other states on the environment and on electricity rates.

decisions.notes: Packet's prior disposition (Veto Sustained, 2026-04-29) fully confirmed via legislature.maine.gov and the House roll call record. Added detail: the House enactment vote (83-66 on 2026-04-08) fell short of the two-thirds override threshold from the start, and the actual override attempt after the veto (roll call 828, 2026-04-29) got 72 yes / 65 no against a 92-vote requirement, so the veto stands sustained. bill_status_category is 'vetoed' per schema guidance (passed the Legislature but veto not overridden).
